actions.reason: C0001 has a coherent RNA-defined biological identity with strong, FDR-significant pathway enrichment in metabolic and coagulation programs, and no dominant measured technical confounder. Cross-modal support is limited but not actively contradictory, and structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. Retaining this discovery-stage candidate is better supported than Drop.

C0002 lacks any FDR-significant biological signal across RNA, WXS, or CNV, with only weak nominal trends and wide confidence intervals. Cross-modal consistency is modest but not sufficient to define a coherent identity, and no structural correction is positively supported. The evidence does not justify retaining this candidate for downstream validation.

C0003 shows a coherent biological identity with significant RNA pathway enrichment (pancreas beta cells, heme metabolism), a strong PBRM1 mutation trend, and a significant CNV feature (chr20q). Although PBRM1 does not survive FDR, the combined evidence is coherent and not dominated by technical factors. No positive structural evidence supports Split or Merge, so Accept is better supported than Drop.

C0004 has a strong, coherent RNA-defined immune-related identity with 16 FDR-significant pathways, including downregulation of inflammatory and immune pathways. WXS and CNV are not significant but do not actively contradict the RNA signal. Technical confounding is not dominant, and structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. Retaining this candidate is better supported than Drop.

C0005 is heavily confounded by multiple technical factors (tissue source site, CT manufacturer, scanner model, reconstruction kernel, slice thickness) that are FDR-significant and plausibly explain the observed molecular differences. Biological support is weak with no significant RNA or CNV findings and only a nominal FLG mutation trend. The measured technical explanation dominates the candidate identity, so Drop is better supported than Accept.

C0006 shows a coherent RNA-defined EMT signal with a large effect size, and nominal BAP1 and TTN mutation enrichment that is biologically plausible. Although not FDR-significant, the small sample size limits power, and the evidence is not actively contradicted by other modalities. Technical confounding is not dominant, and no positive structural evidence supports Split or Merge. Retaining this candidate is better supported than Drop.

C0007 has a strong, coherent RNA-defined inflammatory and myogenesis-suppressed identity with 14 FDR-significant pathways, and a nominal BAP1 mutation enrichment that is biologically plausible. Technical confounding is not dominant, and structural evidence does not positively support Split or Merge. Retaining this candidate is better supported than Drop.

C0008 has only two members, making all biological and structural analyses underpowered and unreliable. No significant findings exist in any modality, and the set is too small to define a coherent identity or assess structural corrections. The evidence is insufficient to justify retaining this candidate for downstream validation.
